nodes.title: ElastiCache cluster has no AUTH token configured
nodes.description: The ElastiCache Redis cluster 'ecommerce-cache' does not require an AUTH token for client authentication. Any client that can reach port 6379 has unrestricted read/write access to all cached data, including session tokens and JWT blacklist entries.

control.name: ElastiCache Redis clusters should require AUTH tokens
control.description: Enabling AUTH for Redis prevents unauthenticated access to cached data.

securitySubCategories.title: Ensure ElastiCache for Redis clusters use encryption in transit and at rest

nodes.title: Security group allows unrestricted inbound access to Redis port 6379
nodes.description: Security group 'ecommerce-cache' (sg-0ec3a92f1d4b78c45) permits inbound TCP traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 6379.

control.name: Security groups should not permit unrestricted access to sensitive ports

nodes.title: ECS task definition does not specify a non-root user
nodes.description: The ECS task definition 'ecommerce-api:8' runs container processes as root (UID 0).

control.name: ECS task definitions should specify a non-root user

nodes.title: ECS task definition contains sensitive environment variables in plaintext
nodes.description: The ECS task definition 'ecommerce-api:8' passes sensitive values (DATABASE_URL, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY) as plaintext environment variables.

control.name: ECS task definitions should use secrets management for sensitive values

nodes.title: RDS security group allows inbound access from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432
nodes.description: Security group 'ecommerce-db' permits inbound TCP traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432 (PostgreSQL).

control.name: RDS security groups should restrict inbound access to known CIDRs

nodes.title: ECS task IAM role grants overly broad S3 permissions
nodes.description: The IAM role 'ecommerce-task-role' attached to the ECS task definition grants s3:* (all actions) on * (all resources). This exceeds the minimum permissions required for application operation and would allow a compromised container to read, write, and delete all S3 objects accessible to the account.

control.name: IAM policies should follow the principle of least privilege
control.description: IAM roles should grant only the minimum permissions required. Wildcard actions and resources should be avoided.

nodes.title: ECS cluster does not enforce IMDSv2 for task metadata requests
nodes.description: The ECS cluster 'ecommerce-cluster' does not set requiresCompatibilities or metadata endpoint options to enforce IMDSv2. Tasks running on this cluster can retrieve AWS instance metadata using IMDSv1, which does not require a session token and is accessible from any process within the container.

control.name: ECS tasks should use IMDSv2 to access instance metadata
control.description: IMDSv2 requires a session-oriented approach using PUT request for tokens, providing protection against SSRF-based credential theft.

nodes.title: WAF inspection rule excludes /api/v1/graphql path from SQL injection pattern matching
nodes.description: The WAF configuration in docs/infrastructure/waf.tf defines a managed rule group override that excludes the path /api/v1/graphql from the AWS-AWSManagedRulesSQLiRuleSet inspection rule. Requests to the GraphQL endpoint bypass SQL injection pattern matching entirely. The exclusion is applied at the URI path level and affects all HTTP methods to that path.

control.name: WAF managed rule group overrides should be reviewed for security impact
control.description: WAF rule exclusions reduce inspection coverage. Path-level exclusions from injection detection rules should be documented and reviewed against the attack surface of the excluded endpoint.

securitySubCategories.title: 6.4.2 - A web application firewall is deployed in front of public-facing web applications

_description: Additional CSPM findings from api-gateway.tf, ecs-task.tf, cloudtrail.tf, secrets-manager.tf

nodes.title: API Gateway route GET /api/v1/users has no JWT authorizer attached
nodes.description: The AWS API Gateway v2 HTTP API (ecommerce-http-api) defines a JWT authorizer (ecommerce-jwt-authorizer) applied to authenticated routes. The route GET /api/v1/users is registered in the public_routes group with authorization_type = NONE. This route returns all user records including email addresses, bcrypt password hashes, reset tokens, OAuth IDs, and role assignments. The OpenAPI specification for this endpoint documents bearerAuth as required. The authorizer is not applied. The application layer has no protect middleware on the route handler.

control.name: API Gateway routes exposing sensitive data should require authorization
control.description: Routes that return PII or account data must have an authorizer configured. Routes registered with authorization_type = NONE bypass all token validation.

nodes.title: API Gateway JWT authorizer validates signature but does not enforce signing key source
nodes.description: The API Gateway JWT authorizer (ecommerce-jwt-authorizer) validates token signature and expiry against the configured Cognito issuer. It does not verify which signing key was used to generate the token. The ECS task definition sets ACCESS_TOKEN_FALLBACK = 'jwt-secret-dev-fallback-2024' as a plaintext environment variable. Tokens signed with this fallback value will pass authorizer validation if the application accepts them at the code level. The authorizer provides no protection against forged tokens signed with the committed fallback secret.

control.name: API Gateway JWT authorizers should be validated against a single authoritative signing key

nodes.title: ECS task definition references Secrets Manager for ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET but retains plaintext ACCESS_TOKEN_FALLBACK in same task
nodes.description: The ECS task definition 'ecommerce-api:12' includes a secrets block that injects ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET from AWS Secrets Manager (ecommerce/prod/jwt-access-token-secret). The same task definition also sets ACCESS_TOKEN_FALLBACK = 'jwt-secret-dev-fallback-2024' as a plaintext environment variable. The application in tokenUtils.ts falls back to ACCESS_TOKEN_FALLBACK if ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is absent at runtime. Secrets Manager adoption is partial: the migration reference exists but the fallback was not removed. A token forged with the committed fallback value is accepted by the application if ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET is unset or if the app logic evaluates the fallback path.

control.name: ECS task definitions should not retain plaintext credential fallbacks alongside Secrets Manager references
control.description: Partial secrets migration where a fallback plaintext value coexists with a Secrets Manager reference creates a degraded-state attack surface. If Secrets Manager injection fails, the application silently falls back to the committed plaintext value.

nodes.title: CloudTrail log file validation is disabled
nodes.description: The CloudTrail trail 'ecommerce-audit-trail' has enable_log_file_validation set to false. Log files delivered to S3 are not cryptographically signed. An attacker who gains S3 write access can modify or delete trail logs without leaving a detectable integrity violation. In combination with the application's unauthenticated DELETE /api/v1/logs endpoint, this means a breach could result in no recoverable audit trail at either the application or infrastructure layer.

control.name: CloudTrail log file validation should be enabled

nodes.title: CloudTrail does not capture global service events (IAM, STS)
nodes.description: The CloudTrail trail 'ecommerce-audit-trail' has include_global_service_events = false. IAM API calls, STS AssumeRole operations, and credential issuance events are not captured. If ECS task credentials are exfiltrated (via SSRF or container compromise) and used externally to call AWS APIs, no CloudTrail record is written for those calls. The forensic trail for credential abuse is absent.

control.name: CloudTrail should capture global service events

nodes.title: Datadog log collection forwards raw JWT access tokens from application logs
nodes.description: The Datadog agent sidecar in the ECS task definition collects all container stdout logs and forwards them to Datadog. The application's protect.ts middleware logs the raw accessToken cookie value and the decoded JWT payload on every authenticated request. The Datadog agent configuration (datadog-agent.yml) does not include scrubbing rules for JWT token values in log message bodies. The WAF redacted_fields configuration covers the HTTP Authorization header at the network layer only — it does not apply to application log content. JWT access tokens for all authenticated users are accessible in Datadog log streams within the 30-second flush interval. Any principal with Datadog log viewer access can harvest live session tokens.

control.name: Log collection agents should scrub credential values from application log content
control.description: Sidecar log collection agents that forward application stdout without scrubbing may inadvertently expose tokens, keys, or credentials written to logs by application code.

nodes.title: WAF rate limit rule scoped to /api/v1/auth/signin only — credential endpoints not covered
nodes.description: The WAF rule 'RateLimit-SignIn' applies a rate limit of 100 requests per 5 minutes to /api/v1/auth/signin only. No rate limit rule covers /api/v1/users, /api/v1/logs, /api/v1/graphql, or other sensitive endpoints. The route GET /api/v1/users returns all 2,847 user records including bcrypt password hashes in a single unauthenticated GET request. A rate limit on this endpoint would not prevent exfiltration (one request is sufficient) but the absence of any coverage reflects incomplete WAF policy design for the full API surface.

control.name: WAF rate limiting should cover all endpoints that expose sensitive data or bulk operations
